conclusions: The control failed at the inventory/reconciliation layer even if the written exclusion policy was sincere.
Point-in-time vetting cannot enforce an eligibility condition that changes after access is granted.
counterarguments: The agencies may not have used Columbus data for immigration enforcement while access remained active.
findings: On July 15, CPD said remaining one-to-one partners did not include 287(g) agencies.
On July 17, CPD removed four current 287(g) agencies after journalists matched public 287(g) records against sharing relationships.
The correction occurred after external discovery, not through a demonstrated continuous internal reconciliation process.
limitations: Full partner list, edge history, and query logs were unavailable in the reviewed public reporting.
data.method: Timeline reconstruction, claim contradiction analysis, and control-plane observability review.
data.question: Did CPD's public description of its narrowed one-to-one sharing network match actual configured access?
recommendations: Obtain edge activation/removal timestamps, administrator identities, and the source used to track 287(g) status.
Implement fail-closed continuous reconciliation with change detection and mandatory recertification.
unresolved: Complete active and historical edge table.
Exact four-agency query activity before removal.
